column3: NKJV repeats “the God of” before Isaac and Jacob, following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has it only before Abraham.
NKJV has “The LORD your God” and adds “Him you shall hear,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “God will raise up.”
NKJV spells the name “Remphan,” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Rephan.”
NKJV has “for the God of Jacob,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “for the house of Jacob.”
NKJV has the singular “heart,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the plural “hearts.”
NKJV supplies “God” as the one Stephen was calling on; the Greek has no object.
